The Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) on Oct. 22 finalized a rule that allows commercial nuclear reactor applicants to use analyses, test data, and other technical evidence from reactor demonstrations previously authorized by the Department of Energy (DOE) or Department of War (DOW) to support license applications.
The measure establishes a more direct means of incorporating federal demonstration results into commercial reactor safety reviews, potentially reducing duplicative technical evaluations as developers seek to move advanced nuclear technologies from testing to commercial deployment.
The final rule , which amends provisions in 10 CFR Parts 50 and 53, explicitly allows applicants to reference prior federal authorizations when demonstrating that a reactor design can perform its required safety functions. While the NRC has historically considered testing, analyses, and operating experience in licensing reviews, the amendments establish a specific regulatory provision for information gathered from reactors that DOE or DOW previously authorized and that have been tested and demonstrated the ability to function safely. The extent to which applicants can rely on that evidence will depend on how closely the demonstration results correspond to the proposed commercial design and whether the information satisfies applicable NRC requirements.
The NRC called the rule the first major change to its reactor regulations finalized under Executive Order (EO) 14300, which President Donald Trump signed on May 23, 2025. Section 5(d) of the order calls for an expedited pathway to approve reactor designs that DOE or DOW have tested and that have demonstrated the ability to function safely. It directs that NRC review of such designs “shall focus solely on risks that may arise from new applications permitted by NRC licensure, rather than revisiting risks that have already been addressed in the DOE or DOD processes.”
“This rule delivers the EO 14300 vision for an expedited path from DOE and DOW projects to NRC commercial licensing,” NRC Chairman Ho K. Nieh said in the agency’s announcement. “High-quality applications showing how DOE and DOW results apply to NRC requirements will help us review them more efficiently.”
A New Licensing Pathway
The amendments establish an additional option for demonstrating reactor safety under the NRC’s existing commercial licensing requirements, including the frameworks established under Parts 50 and 52 and the risk-informed, technology-inclusive framework under Part 53. They do not establish a separate licensing process or exempt developers from the statutory and regulatory requirements that govern commercial nuclear facilities.
Under Part 50, Section 50.43(e) governs the demonstration of safety functions for reactor designs that differ significantly from light-water reactor designs licensed before 1997, or that use simplified, inherent, passive, or other innovative means to accomplish those functions. The existing provisions establish two alternatives: applicants may demonstrate the performance of individual safety features, assess their interdependent effects, and provide sufficient data to validate analytical tools through analyses, testing, or operating experience, or they may rely on acceptable prototype plant testing across specified operating and accident conditions.
The final rule adds Section 50.43(f), which explicitly provides that an application under Section 50.43(e) “may include consideration of relevant information gathered from a utilization facility that has been previously authorized by the Department of Energy or the Department of Defense and that has been tested and has demonstrated the ability to function safely.” The regulatory text retains the “Department of Defense” title for consistency with existing NRC regulations. Applicants must identify how attributes of that prior authorization satisfy NRC regulations, including the safety demonstration requirements established under Section 50.43(e).
A corresponding revision to Section 53.440(a)(1) permits similar use of federal demonstration evidence under Part 53, where applicants must demonstrate that reactor design features can satisfy defined functional criteria for design-basis accidents and other licensing-basis events. Those demonstrations must consider interdependent effects throughout the commercial nuclear plant and the range of conditions under which the relevant safety features must function throughout the plant’s lifetime.
In both cases, the provisions give applicants an additional means of substantiating their safety cases, potentially allowing the NRC to rely on relevant technical evidence already developed through a federal demonstration program. However, the agency emphasized that applicants remain responsible for establishing how prior authorization results satisfy its requirements, including where the demonstrated design differs from the proposed commercial reactor. Those differences could include changes in reactor design, functionality, associated hazards, siting information, or underlying safety assumptions.
The NRC acknowledged this limitation in the final rule, explaining that the scope of a DOE or DOW authorization or associated testing may not fully represent a commercial reactor configuration or the breadth of analyses necessary for an NRC licensing basis. Consequently, applicants may use prior demonstration evidence to satisfy some requirements, but they must address any remaining gaps to ensure full compliance with NRC requirements.
The agency also stressed that the rule does not transfer regulatory authority from the NRC to DOE or DOW or permit the NRC to dispense with its own safety assessments.
“Nothing in this rule delegates to DOE, DOW, or any other agency the NRC’s functions to evaluate a request for NRC approval, and nothing in this rule allows the NRC to forego an independent review,” the final rule states.
The NRC said it will continue to conduct the independent assessments necessary to confirm whether applicants have satisfied requirements under the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 and NRC regulations. However, where an applicant justifies the applicability and relevance of information from a prior DOE or DOW authorization, the agency said it may be able to tailor the focus and depth of its review.
Federal Reactor Demonstrations Already Underway
The new rule comes as DOE and the U.S. Army are advancing separate reactor demonstration programs that could provide technical evidence for future commercial licensing applications. Although neither program automatically qualifies its participants for expedited NRC review, both are generating or preparing to generate the testing, operational, and safety data that developers may eventually seek to use under the new provisions.
DOE’s efforts have already produced several milestones. Following the launch of its Reactor Pilot Program in June 2025 and the selection of 11 initial projects from 10 companies that August, four DOE-authorized reactors achieved zero-power fueled criticality by July 4, 2026, exceeding the three-reactor target established under President Trump’s May 2025 executive order on reactor testing. The demonstrations included Antares Nuclear’s Mark-0 on June 4, Valar Atomics’ Ward 250 on June 18, Deployable Energy’s Unity on June 30, and Aalo Atomics’ Aalo-X Critical Test Reactor on July 4.
The projects advanced through different DOE authorization pathways, however. Deployable Energy’s Unity experiment, for example, proceeded through the Nuclear Energy Launch Pad at Idaho National Laboratory, not the initial Reactor Pilot Program. Meanwhile, Oklo’s Groves Isotope Test Reactor in Lockhart, Texas, became the fifth DOE-authorized reactor to achieve criticality on Aug. 5. That low-power, water-cooled facility supports isotope-production development and is distinct from Oklo’s Aurora commercial power reactor.
While these criticality experiments establish a self-sustaining fission chain reaction and provide valuable reactor-physics data, they do not demonstrate sustained electricity production or the performance of a complete commercial reactor plant. Nevertheless, developers are already examining how the resulting technical evidence could support future licensing.
Meanwhile, the Army is pursuing a more direct route toward electricity production through its Janus Program , developed in partnership with the Defense Innovation Unit (DIU). In August, the Army selected five developers for initial microreactor projects at military installations: Antares Nuclear at Fort Bragg, North Carolina; BWXT Advanced Technologies at Fort Campbell, Kentucky; General Atomics Electromagnetic Systems at Fort Hood, Texas; Radiant Industries at Fort Benning, Georgia; and Westinghouse Government Services at Fort Drum, New York.
Under the initiative, the Army plans to commit up to $2.2 billion through milestone-based agreements spanning fiscal years 2027 through 2031. The contractor-owned and operated reactors are intended to supply reliable electricity to military installations, and the Army is targeting operation of at least one reactor by Sept. 30, 2028, consistent with the deployment objective established under Executive Order 14299. The program is also intended to support the development of commercially marketable microreactor technologies, although the Army does not expect all five initial projects to begin operating by that deadline.
The Army Reactor Regulatory Office will oversee safety authorizations for the defense reactors, creating another potential source of federally evaluated reactor performance data. For developers seeking to deploy similar technologies commercially, however, those authorizations will not replace NRC licensing. The extent to which they can support future applications will depend on the relevance of the demonstration evidence and the developers’ ability to address differences in reactor configurations, operating conditions, sites, and associated hazards.
The NRC’s final rule will take effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register, which the agency expects during the week of Oct. 26.

The Largest Christensen Superyacht Ever Built Is Ready to Change Hands for $28M
33 photos
Photo: Denison Yachting
The most exciting event for superyacht lovers worldwide is coming up – the 2026 Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show (FLIB) – and one of the stars of the show is not a brand-new release, but one of the greatest builds by one of the top American yacht builders of all time, and it comes with special perks.
The United States (alongside Russia) is still at the top of the list when it comes to luxury yacht buyers, and although it could be argued that its superyacht-building industry isn’t where it should be right now, it’s still up there in terms of great luxury yachts built over time.
Many of the richest and most influential American celebrities choose Northern European shipyards that specialize in megayachts and innovative, groundbreaking design and engineering, but there are countless floating luxury toys available right here, in the US, boasting not only proven quality but the unique appeal of American shipbuilding heritage.
Silver Lining is exactly one-decade-old but it’s an excellent alternative to any new-build in the same size category (50 meters/164 feet). It will be present at this year’s Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show, coming up on October 28, and it promises to be one of the most coveted pre-loved models.
Photo: Denison Yachting This is not just one of the most impressive Christensen yachts, but the largest from this builder in terms of volume. At 164 feet, Silver Lining offers a massive 570 GT volume, translating to approximately 14 per cent more than the standard 499 GT benchmark for this size category. It is emphatically, but rightly described as “a 170-footer in disguise”, meaning that it offers the volume of a considerably larger yacht within a smaller frame.
It packs 11,000 square feet (1,000 square meters) from top to bottom and a luxurious configuration of six huge staterooms for up to 12 guests – which is not common for a 50-meter yacht. Built in 2016 and officially launched in 2017, Silver Lining became an instant American icon.
It’s said to have been originally owned by billionaire Forrest Preston, the man who founded Life Care Centers of America back in the 1970s, and is reportedly currently owned by real estate mogul JD Nichols. Whoever the current owner is, he had to be wealthy enough to deal with what can become one of the biggest hurdles for any experienced luxury yacht owner – the ten-year survey.
The ten-year anniversary of a luxury yacht means that it needs to complete a classification survey. This is a very thorough evaluation of all structural and mechanical components – anything that isn’t up to standard must be repaired or replaced in order to pass the evaluation. A yacht that already successfully completed its ten-year survey is officially ready for the next decade with no need for further investments.
Photo: Denison Yachting In this case, Silver Lining has completed this milestone (its ten-year ABS/American Bureau of Shipping survey) this year, right in time for FLIB, where it will be looking for a new owner. Plus, it has undergone a significant refit in accordance with this survey, said to be worth around $1.3 million. In other words, its current owner had to pump more than $1 million in his pleasure craft this year alone, before he was able to bring it to the market.
This is excellent news for the future owner, because he’s practically getting a freshly-recertified, refitted luxury yacht that doesn’t need any extra money put into it, unless the new owner wants to tweak the interior style. Of course, we can’t ignore the intimidating $27.9 million price tag, but the 2026 ten-year ABS survey and refit are perks that make this yacht valuable beyond the price tag.
Following the refit, Silver Lining emerged with realigned engines and new engine mounts, rebuilt stabilizers, overhauled running gear, and a fresh bottom coating.
Style-wise, Silver Lining is a beautiful modern-classic flaunting the kind of elegance that makes a yacht timeless. Kimberly Graham was behind this elegant design centered around high-gloss Black Walnut woodwork that evokes classic American ocean liners, marble finishes, and precious textiles. A neutral color palette highlighted by the Black Walnut paneling is complemented by old-school mirrors and golden accents.
Photo: Denison Yachting A full-beam main-deck owner’s suite is the crown pearl, boasting vast spaces for separate his-and-her bathrooms, two walk-in closets, and a private office. Two other huge staterooms (king-sized) and two guest cabins with twin beds and Pullman berths ensure flexible accommodation both for private cruising or commercial charter.
Spacious amenities and living spaces throughout make Silver Lining particularly attractive for families or large groups of guests in general. The main salon offers formal dining for 12, while the bridge deck provides a perfect area for al-fresco dining, complete with adjustable wind protection, heating, and cooling. Notable amenities also include the eight-person jacuzzi on the sundeck, with an aft touch-and-go helipad.
Starlink connectivity and an ABS-approved, 300-gallon auxiliary fuel tank for tender or helicopter operations are some of the more recent perks. Twin MTU engines and four Caterpillar generators keep Silver Lining cruising comfortably at 14 knots, with a maximum range of 4,000 nautical miles at an economical speed of nine knots.
Quantum zero-speed stabilizers keep things comfortable for the onboard guests, and even the yacht’s original bulbous bow helps make the cruising experience smoother and more efficient. Silver Lining also comes with a proven charter track record, and is currently licensed for up to 84 days per calendar year.
Photo: Denison Yachting This means that the future owner could start making money from this investment pretty much right after the purchase, and that’s huge, because a luxury yacht this size gobbles up several millions per year just in fuel and maintenance.
Silver Lining was one of those superyachts that stayed away from the spotlight, meaning that they had discrete owners, but some of the Christensen yachts built in the same era became instantly famous thanks to their celebrity owners. The 155-footer Privacy, launched in 2004, is owned by none other than Tiger Woods, and the 195-foot Casino Royale, launched in 2008, was built for John Staluppi and designed by Staluppi together with Carol Williamson & Associates.
Dave Christensen, the man behind Christensen Yachts, passed away in 2018, leaving behind one of the most successful and acclaimed luxury yacht builders in America. He founded Christensen Shipyards in 1986, after retiring from a successful career in the construction industry, and the young shipyard went on to specialize in custom composite superyachts, with hundreds of pleasure craft launched to this day.
In the early ‘80s, when he couldn’t find the builder that would create exactly the kind of yacht he dreamed of, this visionary man decided to build one himself. He partnered with Westport Shipyard for the hull, then completed the rest on his own. With this first yacht, came the decision to launch a yacht building company, and the rest is history.
Photo: Denison Yachting To this day, Silver Lining remains the largest Christensen yacht ever built (in terms of volume) and the recent ten-year milestone means it’s ready for at least another decade of smooth cruising and unrivaled onboard comfort for guests. This iconic American yacht is currently asking for $27.9 million and it’s safe to say that it will attract a lot of potential buyers at the upcoming Fort Lauderdale International Boat Show starting next week.

BYD will open pre-orders for the Denza N8 EV next week, a large five-seat luxury electric SUV with a CLTC range of over 623 miles (1,000 km).
BYD Denza N8 EV launches in November
The Denza N8 initially went on sale in China in 2023 as a mid-to-large-size luxury SUV. It was available as a plug-in hybrid (PHEV) with six- and seven-seat configurations.
BYD is preparing to introduce an all-electric version that will deliver the same electric-only driving range as the PHEV did on a full charge and full tank of gas, combined.
“The king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles,” as Denza calls it, will use BYD’s second-generation Blade Batteries and Flash Charging Technology. The setup delivers “a world-leading 1,003 km pure electric range,” under CLTC conditions, Denza claimed.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
BYD’s 1,500 kW Flash Charging tech powers compatible vehicles from 10% to 70% in just five minutes. To go from 10% to 97%, it takes only nine minutes.
Li Hui, Denza’s general manager, announced on Weibo on October 22 that the company plans to open pre-orders for the Denza N8 EV on October 26, with the official launch in November.
Denza’s general manager li Hui confirms pre-orders for the N8 will open on October 26, with an official launch in November (Source: Li Hui/Weibo)
According to a regulatory filing released by China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) in August, the Denza N8 EV is 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase.
The Denza N8 EV will use a massive 130.15 kWh battery, providing a pure electric CLTC range of up to 623 miles (1,003 km).
BYD will offer a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD version uses a single motor producing either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp).
The tri-motor Denza N8, meanwhile, is based on BYD’s e3 platform. The setup includes a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, delivering a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).
Denza N8 interior (Source: Denza)
Inside, the luxury SUV features two huge digital screens. One 30″ center infotainment screen spans nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard, and a new 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) sits below the windshield.
Like many new BYD models, the cabin adopts a minimalist design with premium features like ambient lighting, a three-spoke steering wheel, and higher-end materials.
Ahead of its official launch, the Denza N8 EV was spotted in China undisguised. New images from Autohome show the luxury SUV driving in public, with roof-mounted LiDAR and a sleek, premium look.
Last month, BYD also launched the Denza N8L EV , a slightly longer six-seat version of the current PHEV sold in China.
BYD Denza N8L EV (Source: BYD)
The Denza N8L EV is available in two versions. The N8L EV Premium starts at 299,800 yuan, or about $45,000, while the Flagship model is priced from 329,800 yuan ($49,000).
Both versions use a 130.15 kWh BYD Blade Battery 2.0, providing a CLTC range of up to 596 miles (960 km).

With the EPA ‘27 engine rules impacting nitrogen oxide (NoX) emissions in heavy duty vehicles getting closer every day, the new rules will have a major impact on anybody who buys new vehicles…like Ryder.
Ryder’s (NYSE: R) third quarter earnings released early Thursday were solid enough that it propelled the stock up 10.49% to $265.53, a gain of 25.22%. It is still below its 52-week high of $284.25 set on June 12.
With the strong quarter in the books leading to a discussion on the company’s earnings call with analysts about its growth prospects, the concurrent issue is what will be Ryder’s strategy to power that growth with new vehicles.
Ryder’s new truck purchases work side-by-side with its activity in its ChoiceLease business, which is the longer-term leasing of vehicles (as opposed to its Rental segment, which are for shorter-term arrangements.) The price of a new vehicle can kick back into the actions of customers, as one analyst noted who asked on the call, “Are your customers hesitant to be placing orders for ‘27 now? Does this impact you?”
No buying yet
Ryder CEO John Diez said the company had not seen any sort of “pre-buy surge activity with the change in technology.” But that doesn’t mean it isn’t part of the planning process.
Tom Havens, who is the president of Ryder’s Fleet Management Solutions, which includes its leasing and rental activities, said “it’s pretty well understood at this point that price increases are coming in 2027. And despite that, there was not any significant prebuy activity” in the quarter.
Some customers “took advantage of it, but not to any large extent,” Havens added.
Buying EPA ‘27 compliant vehicles now faces the problem of not knowing what the final rule will be. The EPA has rolled out an amendment process to the initial rule , including such measures as noncompliance penalties and a change in the “deratement” rules that would slow or stop a vehicle if its levels of diesel exhaust fluid got too low.
Fleet numbers lower than normal
Analyst Jeffrey Kauffman of Citizens JMP Securities noted that Ryder’s data on the size of its fleet has been below historic norms, particularly for tractors. Adding new tractors, Kauffman said, “is going to be kind of tough over the next six to nine months just because of the EPA mandate.” He asked whether Ryder had secured an adequate number of “slots” with OEMs to fill any increase in the company’s demand.
Diez said Ryder is “confident we can grow that fleet.” He also said Ryder has “already taken action in the quarter of starting to bring in equipment,” which Diez added is visible in the company’s capital expenditure budget.
But Diez cautioned that utilization of the Ryder fleet “is not yet to screaming red levels like we saw post-COVID, but it will get there if we don’t have fleet, and we’re going to continue adding to meet that demand.”
The rental fleet had utilization of 77% in the quarter, compared to 70% a year ago. For the nine months, that figure stands at 73%. In the second quarter of 2022, the peak of the post-COVID surge, it was 81.6%.
Used vehicle sales remain a key driver of Ryder earnings. Diez noted that current inventories of used vehicles at Ryder are at 7,300, which he said is at the low end of the company’s target range of 7,000. They were 8,500 a year ago.
The structure at $R has changed over the years and it is less reliant on used vehicle sales as a driver in its earnings. But it's still important, and in the third quarter, it was a big benefit to the bottom line. pic.twitter.com/kk7eldScpC — John Kingston (@JohnHKingston) October 22, 2026
“We’re going to continue to sell through that inventory,” Diez said. The used vehicle market remains tight enough that Diez said Ryder would expect to sell more of its used vehicles through retail rather than wholesale channels, which is generally more profitable. Retail sales accounted for 61% of all used vehicle sales in the quarter, according to Ryder data, compared to 54% in the third quarter a year ago and 56% sequentially with the second quarter.
Bigger retail footprint
But Diez forecast that the retail number will cross the 70% mark in 2027. “We have that lever for us based on the thin inventories we expect to face later next year,” he said. “That’s the biggest hedge against market forces.”
Diez noted that the company had forecast a $40 million used vehicle gain for the year, which would have been up $20 million from 2025. But now with the used vehicle market at its current levels, the CEO projected that the full-year gain on used vehicle sales will be $50 million to $60 million.
Diez wrapped up the equipment discussion on the call by saying that “when we get back together (on the fourth quarter earnings call), we’ll give you a look at the full year for 2027.”
Ryder’s Dedicated Transportation Solutions (DTS) segment is the window into the market for drivers, as it needs to either hire new drivers to service its dedicated customers or take steps to retain the drivers at companies whose fleet responsibilities have been turned over to DTS.
John Sensing, the president of both DTS and contract logistics segment Supply Chain Solutions (SCS), said DTS has been seeing “about a mid to single digit wage increase in certain regions” at DTS.
The unit has what Sensing called “annual CPI openers” that passes on wage increases directly to customers. But he added there also are “driver wage indices” used by Ryder “that allow us if we see a drastic change to go back and open discussions with these customers.”
Sensing also stressed that Ryder’s experience in the driver market is not necessarily indicative of the broader competition for drivers. The DTS operation often works in highly specialized areas, he said, and “80% of our jobs are home every day or every night. So that’s very attractive.”

source_document.body:
Tesla skipped one of its top shareholder questions on its Q3 2026 earnings call: when Hardware 3 owners will find out if they get a free computer upgrade for the unsupervised “Full Self-Driving” they paid for.
The question ranked fifth by shares on Say. Tesla read and answered questions ranked below it. It went past this one without a word.
Tesla went down the list and around HW3
Tesla takes retail shareholder questions through the Say platform before every earnings call, and shareholders upvote them with their shares. When we previewed the Q3 2026 earnings as submissions closed, the HW3 question sat fifth with 557 votes and 652,900 shares.
Here’s how it was worded:
Advertisement - scroll for more content
“Tesla has acknowledged that HW3 vehicles cannot support unsupervised FSD. When will owners know whether they can upgrade their hardware for free, and when will Tesla provide a clear plan?”
Head of investor relations Travis Axelrod read nine Say questions on Wednesday’s call. Tesla answered the Cybercab scaling question, unsupervised FSD in customer cars, Cybercab ownership, and robotaxi and Optimus unit economics. Then it went on to questions about Optimus training data, Optimus revenue, FSD mapping, and factory production rates.
The Optimus revenue and FSD mapping questions both ranked below HW3 in every ranking published before the call. The Optimus training data one didn’t even make the top 10.
Axelrod closed the segment with “That’s it for the Say.com questions.” No analyst asked about HW3 either, and HW3, AI3, or a retrofit didn’t come up once during the entire call.
The skipped question is the other half of the one Tesla answered
The second question Tesla took was “When can we anticipate FSD unsupervised in customer cars?”
Ashok Elluswamy, Tesla’s head of AI, answered that the same software running in Model Y robotaxis and the Cybercab will come to customers with FSD v15, and that “somewhere around Q2 next year” the first customer vehicles could join the Robotaxi fleet.
That’s another delay, a new timeline that history suggests will likely be pushed back, and an HW4 answer. Musk admitted on the Q1 2026 call that “Hardware 3 simply does not have the capability to achieve unsupervised FSD,” citing an eighth of HW4’s memory bandwidth. So every time Tesla gives a date for unsupervised FSD, it’s a date that doesn’t apply to millions of cars Tesla sold as having all the hardware needed for full self-driving.
And HW3 owners have been promised something by Musk on each of the last two calls. In April, he talked about “microfactories” in major cities to swap computers and cameras, and a discounted trade-in. In July, when a Truist analyst asked about it, Musk said upgrading would make sense “at some point” and floated skipping HW4 for a next-gen board or AI5, which goes to Optimus first.
No cost, no timeline, no process. And this quarter, not even a mention.
Tesla’s legal exposure on HW3 keeps growing
Tesla sold FSD for up to $15,000 on the promise that its cars already had the hardware. Now it’s facing class actions in the US, China, and Australia, and a Dutch collective claim that grew to nearly 7,000 HW3 owners with a law firm behind it. Documents from Dutch regulator RDW show Tesla only submitted HW4 for FSD approval in Europe.
HW3 owners got a stripped-down FSD v14 “Lite” this year. It’s a supervised driver assist, and it doesn’t come close to what they bought.
Electrek’s Take
We don’t think this was an accident. Tesla picks which Say questions it reads and in what order, and it chose to answer a question about Optimus revenue it said it had “kind of already answered” over one backed by 650,000 shares about the product its customers already paid for.
Any answer Tesla gives on HW3 has a dollar figure attached, and it’s probably a big one: replacing the computer and cameras in what we estimate to be around 4 million cars, or compensating owners. Every statement on it can also end up quoted in court. Saying nothing is cheaper, at least this quarter.
But Tesla can’t have it both ways. It can’t tell shareholders that unsupervised FSD is coming to customer cars by Q2 2027 while ignoring the owners who bought that exact feature years ago and whose cars will never get it. Many of them paid up to $15,000 upfront for it.
The HW3 upgrade isn’t an engineering problem at this point. Musk already said the hardware can’t do it. It’s a question of whether Tesla will pay to honor what it sold, and right now the answer looks like silence. Will an HW3 owner ever get a real plan before a judge forces one? I bet on nope.

Daimler Truck North America has filed a lawsuit against a former employee and his wife, accusing them of embezzling nearly $3.8 million from the commercial truck manufacturer over a five year period.
The lawsuit, filed Oct. 12 in Washington County Circuit Court in Oregon, names former Daimler employee Terry S. Watson and his wife, Krystal Watson, as defendants. The case, No. 26CV57242, remains open, according to court records reviewed by FreightWaves.
Daimler is seeking approximately $6.6 million in damages in connection with the alleged scheme, according to The Oregonian/OregonLive .
Watson worked in Daimler’s test fleet operations in Portland from 2016 until November 2025, when he was terminated after the company discovered suspicious financial activity, according to published reports.
The company alleges Watson used corporate credit cards and falsified expense reports to pay for personal expenses, including vacations to Europe, Las Vegas and Legoland, as well as landscaping, household services, child care and restaurant deliveries.
The lawsuit also accuses Watson of using company fuel cards for personal purchases and directing contractors to bill Daimler for construction and landscaping work performed at his Hillsboro, Oregon, residence.
Krystal Watson allegedly participated in the scheme by using company credit cards for personal purchases and providing receipts to her husband that were used in falsified expense reports, according to KOIN’s reporting on the lawsuit .
FreightWaves has requested a copy of the original complaint from Washington County Circuit Court. The allegations described in published reports have not been independently verified against the complaint by FreightWaves.
Daimler Truck North America, headquartered in Portland, manufactures commercial vehicles under the Freightliner, Western Star and Thomas Built Buses brands, among others.
Why it matters: The Daimler Truck North America lawsuit raises questions about internal financial controls at one of North America’s largest commercial truck manufacturers after an alleged five-year misuse of corporate funds.

1959 DeSoto Seville Is Not a Cadillac, but an Ultra-Rare Spring Special Mopar
13 photos
Photo: Charles Phoenix/YouTube
Seville is the capital of the autonomous region of Andalusia in southern Spain. To us car gearheads, it's also an iconic nameplate used by Cadillac between 1975 and 2004. But what if I told you that DeSoto also sold a vehicle sporting the Seville badge?
Don't worry if you haven't heard about it; it was a very short-lived model. And the fact that DeSoto hasn't been around for decades doesn't help either. In fact, I'd better refresh your memory before moving forward with this unknown model.
Named after Spanish explorer Hernando de Soto, the marque was established by Walter Chrysler in August 1928. It was founded three years after Walter created the Chrysler Corporation and introduced it alongside the Plymouth division. Both DeSoto and Plymouth were part of Chrysler's plan to divide its vehicle offering by price class.
Plymouth became the entry-level product, while DeSoto slotted between the latter and Dodge, which Chrysler purchased in 1928. DeSoto's initial role was to compete against carmakers like Studebaker, Hudson, and Pontiac in the mid-price class. In 1933, DeSoto was repositioned above Dodge and given access to some Chrysler body styles .
DeSoto went on to produce a version of the pioneering Airflow in 1933 and introduced the first mass-produced American car with pop-up headlamps in 1942. In the 1950s, it debuted the Adventurer, a limited-production, high-performance model similar to the exclusive Chrysler 300 letter series.
The division was phased out in late 1960, mainly due to low sales and overlapping with Chrysler's then-new and lower-priced Newport.
As for the Seville model you probably never knew existed, it was offered in 1959 as a Spring Special model. What's that, you ask? Well, it was common at the time for carmakers to offer mid-year promotional packages to boost dealership traffic and sales during the peak spring car-buying season. The Seville was a package that included various features. It was available on both the Firesweep and Firedome series .
This car is based on the Firesweep, which debuted in 1957 as an entry-level model. The Seville bundle included distinct exterior color configurations, a checkered upholstery pattern, and extra premium appointments such as a padded dashboard and color-keyed steering wheel. It also added "Seville" badges on the rear fenders.
The Seville you see here has a white over light blue exterior and a checkered interior in three-tone turquoise/gray, with darker turquoise stripes and white vinyl. And the really big deal here is that it's been restored to factory specifications and looks downright stunning inside and out.
The engine bay is just as gorgeous and houses the original 361-cubic-inch (5.9-liter) V8 engine. The mill was originally rated at 295 horsepower and 390 pound-feet (529 Nm) of torque and mated with Chrysler's popular three-speed TorqueFlite automatic transmission.
In addition to being a spectacular sight, this DeSoto is also super rare. The company didn't keep records on Spring Special models, but experts say that the bundle found its way on only a tiny fraction of the Firesweeps built that year (due to its short-lived availability).
DeSoto produced 20,834 Firesweeps in 1969, and only 5,481 examples were two-door hardtops like the car you see here. Our host says that "only 2 or 3 are known to exist," and we might be looking at the finest one out there. Check it out in the video below.

Tiny House Lucile Is What an Idyllic Little Castle on Wheels Looks Like
11 photos
Photo: Tiny and Projet Bois
There’s nothing more charming than a French castle, and a miniature version on wheels is even more adorable. This type of charm and elegance aren’t about luxurious amenities, expensive materials, and opulent décor. What makes a tiny house on wheels feel like a castle is the idyllic ambiance, the unique qualities of its shape and craftsmanship (as opposed to industrial templates), and the absolute freedom of personal style – one of the greatest riches.
In some parts of the worlds, like Australia and New Zealand, tiny house design has evolved to be highly practical, functional, and contemporary (style-wise). Rugged metallic shells that look like industrial containers are built to withstand harsh environments while not breaking the bank, and ultra-functional interiors with smart layouts and affordable, industrial furniture help keep things low-cost and low-maintenance.
This specific approach certainly has its undisputed advantages and it can often be a life-saver in the context of acute housing crises, natural disasters, or other social-economic factors. In some European places, like France and Germany, a different approach predominates. Here, tiny homes on wheels are still built with wooden frames, natural timber claddings, and their interiors are almost entirely custom-crafted woodwork.
French tiny homes maintain a traditional silhouette, along with artisan woodwork and minimalism not in the contemporary sense, but more as the common-sense simplicity of our ancestors. Cheap materials, artificial paints, industrial furniture, and formal décor are all ditched in the favor of raw timber, basic appliances, cabin-like interiors, and rustic style.
Photo: Tiny and Projet Bois Lucile’s little castle on wheels may seem too modest from a modern perspective, but its simple, nonchalant elegance will be appreciated by those who embrace sustainability and natural living. She was one of the many city folks who one day made the bold decision leave the city for the good and start living in a tiny house somewhere in the countryside.
For Lucile, this meant leaving the city of Lion and moving to the idyllic countryside of the l’Ain region, where her partner and her found a little plot of land. This specific area was shared by people with a common vision and dedicated entirely to lightweight, alternative houses. That is what Lucile wanted – to begin living more intentionally, simpler, and closer to nature every day.
She worked closely with Jean-Maxime for her custom-built tiny castle, and was very happy with the result. Jean-Maxime himself was once a bold dreamer who left behind a career in environmental engineering to become a full-time carpenter and tiny house builder. The workshop he founded more than a decade ago, Tiny & Projet Bois, is entirely dedicated to woodwork in the broadest sense, from fully livable tiny homes to decks, pergolas, staircases, and furniture.
Lucile’s tiny house is only 6.6-meters long (21.6 feet). The gable roof and the large transom-shaped rear window give it the elegance of a tiny castle with the modern addition of sliding glass doors at the entrance. The light gray shade of the aluminum window frames and roofing was specifically chosen to keep the burning sun away during summer and therefore help keep a cooler ambiance inside.
Photo: Tiny and Projet Bois All of this is combined with traditional timber cladding in a natural tone that makes Lucile’s house blend in beautifully with the natural surroundings. This tiny abode seems to become one with its environment while also providing comfort for its dwellers.
Comfort is defined in a more rustic manner inside this tiny house. Warmth comes from a modest wood-burning stove that sits close to the entrance, at the base of the staircase, where the builder arranged a dedicated area with special insulation and space for storing wood logs. During cold winter evenings, this rustic fireplace creates the perfect ambiance for the cozy lounge – a fairytale cocoon.
The oversized triangular window that makes Lucile’s tiny house remarkable from the outside also gives a majestic elegance to the tiny lounge inside. It visually attracts the eye upwards and outside, creating the illusion of greater spaciousness. During the day, it allows for more natural light to fill the space, which ensures that this home stays bright and airy despite the compact size with not that many windows.
In addition to the tiny sofa leaning against the wall, this lounge features a desk area intended to serve multiple functions. What looks like a plain console with added drawers on each side for extra storage hides a pop-up extension in the center, which turns into a large table. With seats on each side, this becomes an excellent little dining area, with a lovely window view and extra romance thanks to the fireplace nearby.
Photo: Tiny and Projet Bois At the same time, this small corner can be used as a personal workspace (it gets enough natural light from the windows nearby and it allows a welcomed separation between the lounge/relaxation area and the home office area). With its versatile multi-functionality, this tiny desk is also strategically placed between the lounge and the kitchen – close enough to each of them, and also doubling as a buffer zone.
The staircase that leads to the home’s only bedroom also provides most of the storage space for the entire house. It features built-in drawers and cabinets all across, from smaller ones at the base to full-size closets near the bathroom. This allows flexible functionality – the owners can choose to turn some of the bigger closets into a pantry area, a wardrobe, or even a laundry area.
A two-section kitchen is a practical alternative to the fancy kitchens of luxury tiny homes. It provides extra countertop space compared to a compact kitchen, and it doubles the storage space as well. In terms of looks, it’s not that sophisticated (neither is the bathroom, which boasts the typical Nordic sauna look of French tiny homes bathrooms because of the timber wood paneling throughout and the rustic eco-friendly toilet).
Lucile’s tiny house is decorated very simply, and is shows off a certain bohemian touch, mostly thanks to the hanging potted plants and the tiny floating shelves scattered around. The loft bedroom is hidden behind a dramatic red curtain – a more affordable and more convenient alternative to the standard safety walls or railings. Behind the curtains, there’s enough floor space for a two-person bed, flanked by large windows that keep the room bright and airy.
Photo: Tiny and Projet Bois The black window frames are the only accents that add visual contrast to this warm, natural wood interior. Some of the furnishings add bold pops of color, but don’t compete with the natural tone of the timber, which is the star of the show. The natural warmth of wood is what defines this interior, from the panels, floors, and ceiling to the custom-crafted furniture.
Fully equipped with the basics, cool in the summer and toasty in winter – this little gem feels beautiful and cozy year-round, and that’s what matters the most.
Who says that a dream castle must be filled with premium finishes, heavy ornaments and carry a hefty price tag? Personal castles can come in all shapes and sizes, on wheels or without them, and furnished in original ways. In the end, what matters the most is personal freedom, individual style, and the cozy ambiance that can make even the simplest, smallest wooden cabin on wheels feel like the perfect home.

Photo: sonnen
Residential battery storage maker sonnen is reporting two very different stories today: Its German business has filed for insolvency, while sonnen USA says sales have doubled and it’s preparing to expand.
The insolvency filing comes just two months after Shell sold sonnen to investment group TIVEN. Germany’s Handelsblatt reported that sonnen GmbH confirmed the filing and informed roughly 400 employees in Wildpoldsried, Bavaria, on October 22.
For homeowners with sonnen batteries, the immediate question is what happens to service. According to Handelsblatt , the company intends to keep supporting its more than 150,000 existing customers. But a substantial overhaul is coming: Numerous subsidiaries are expected to be wound down or enter insolvency proceedings under self-administration, with only one production site remaining. The report does not identify that site.
Meanwhile, sonnen USA’s announcement describes a growing home battery business. The company says sales have doubled and production has tripled year over year, supported by expanded manufacturing in Stone Mountain, Georgia. It expects to deliver more than 180 megawatt-hours of residential battery storage in 2026.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Much of that growth comes from virtual power plants (VPPs). These connect home batteries so they can work together to support the grid, giving households another way to earn value from their solar and storage systems.
In Texas, sonnen says its SOLRITE offering serves more than 6,000 homes, combining rooftop solar, batteries, energy management, and VPP participation. In Massachusetts, its sonnenCommunity program offers cash rewards to participating homeowners in National Grid and Eversource territories. The company also reports rising sales through its Wattsmart program in Utah.
TIVEN bought the entire global business, including sonnen USA. US CEO Blake Richetta stated today that “TIVEN is firmly committed to the long-term success of sonnen USA as a strong, market-leading company in the North American VPP energy market.”
TIVEN stated that it “looks forward to bolstering the company’s impressive growth.”
But the US announcement leaves an important question unanswered: How will the German restructuring affect the US operation and its customers? It doesn’t address the insolvency filing, and sonnen USA declined to comment on developments in Germany when contacted by pv magazine .
The US growth figures show demand for sonnen’s batteries. What customers still need is a clear explanation of how manufacturing, software support, and service will be maintained through the restructuring.

Chery has announced a 1.44 megawatt charging system, able to deliver 500km (311 miles) in 5 minutes. And it’s not even the fastest system available in China.
It’s become common knowledge at this point that Chinese EVs are the world’s state of the art, but the country isn’t sitting on its laurels, it’s still racing to compete with newer and better technology.
A case in point has been the country’s DC fast chargers, where we’ve seen a slew of announcements of new systems in just the last year.
BYD has a 1.5MW charger which it has already installed 10,000 of , Geely just announced a 2.2MW charger , and CATL has a hyper-fast charging battery .
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The competition is so fierce that firms are starting to compete over seconds, not minutes of charging time.
And now, a new challenger appears: Chery.
Chery announced a 1.44MW charger that can add 500km (311miles) of range to a battery in 5 minutes, and can charge from 10-97% in 6 minutes and 50 seconds, as reported by CarNewsChina .
The numbers put it in league with the best of the best in the country. Per CarNewsChina’s accounting, the new Chery “Volt-Dragon” battery is the second-fastest at reaching 97% state of charge, 23 seconds behind CATL’s 6 minute, 27 second record time. FAW, Geely and BYD are all between 8 and 9 minutes for the same full charge metric.
Some other firms released times for charging in very cold or very warm weather, which Chery declined to release during its announcement. Though it did say that it could still deliver 500km of range in 8 minutes in “conservative scenarios.”
In Chery’s announcement, it dropped the same buzzword as Geely did : “AI-Powered.” Chery calls its system CheryMind, and supposedly it adjusts charging power based on temperature changes within the battery, to help maintain optimal charging speeds and battery health.
Meanwhile in the US, the fastest public chargers are around 400kW, with 750kW potentially coming next year . That’s all plenty quick enough for refueling, especially on a roadtrip , but for high-throughput DC charging locations, especially those in urban areas where some people might not have a consistent parking spot to charge in (and yes, we need to fix that ), higher speed chargers can relieve a lot of pressure.
Chery has only just started installing chargers, and says it will have 100 chargers open in 10 Chinese cities soon. It plans to install 20,000 stations worldwide by 2029, which is quite a bit slower than BYD’s target to have 20,000 chargers installed by the end of this year.

Jay Leno Drives a Smoking, Shaking 1902 Packard, Proves 12 Horses Are Good Enough for LA
27 photos
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube
The first- and last-generation Packards have been parked in Jay Leno’s Garage. The "grandpa" and "grandson" have been shipped across the country all the way from Newport, Rhode Island, where they have been residing in the Audrain Auto Museum, to Los Angeles, California, to be on Jay Leno's show.
The one who accompanies the Packards is Donald Osborne, Classic and Exotic Car Appraiser and Consulting Director of the museum. The grandpa is a 1902 Packard Model F, one of the four known to have survived, while the grandson is the 1956 Packard Caribbean .
The story of the Packard automobiles dates way back. The company was founded in 1899 in Warren, Ohio, by brothers James Ward and William Doud Packard, and their business partner, George Lewis Weiss.
It all started after James Ward Packard bought a car from the Winton Motor Carriage Company in Cleveland. Unhappy with its frequent mechanical failures, he went to give his honest feedback to Alexander Winton. Winton told him to build a better car. And that is exactly what he did.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube The trio completed its very first motor car, the Packard Model A, in 1899. They originally operated under the umbrella of their already existing electrical and wire-making business in Ohio. Before the company relocated, wealthy investor Henry Bourne Joy bought an early Packard and absolutely loved it.
Big in Detroit He traveled to Ohio to meet its creators. Realizing the company needed major capital growth, Joy and a group of investors financed the business, leading to the company reorganizing as the Packard Motor Car Company in 1902 and physically relocating to Detroit, Michigan, in 1903.
That is the era the 1902 Packard Model F comes from. The Model F dropped as somewhat of a revolutionary car at the time, a massive shift from the fragile "horseless carriage" that Packard used to build before. It was, however, the final single-cylinder vehicle that the company produced.
That single-cylinder engine was a massive, four-stroke 184-cubic-inch (3.0-liter) unit, which produced 12 horsepower. It idled at a very low 200 rpm and redlined at just 800 rpm, pushing the car to a top speed of 30 mph (48 kph).
A three-speed Selective Sliding-Gear Transmission with an "H-pattern" shift layout put the power down through those fragile-looking rear wheels. Still, they were far more solid than the flimsy bicycle-style wire wheels of the previous Packards.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Speaking of which, the open-top model rode on 14-spoke artillery wood wheels equipped with 33 x 4-inch pneumatic tires. The Model F also implemented the steering wheel as we know it today, while many vehicles of the era still used steering tillers, similar to those of a boat rudder.
Ford F-150 Raptor money The Model F was Packard's most expensive model in 1902, aimed exclusively at wealthy buyers. It came in two flavors: the two-seat open-air variant priced at $2,250, and the four- or five-passenger versions, which started at $2,500, the equivalent of approximately $77,000 today, which is nearly Ford F-150 Raptor money.
To prove that cars were practical for long-distance traveling and not just short-trip toys, a modified Model F named "Old Pacific" completed the famous San Francisco-to-New York cross-country route. It took the Packard employee 61 days to reach his destination. There were no roads, no maps, not to mention navigation…
Packard built only 179 units of the Model F across 1902 and 1903. Today, only four original examples are known to have survived, which makes them priceless collectibles.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Fast forward to 1956, and Packard rolls out the final model, the Caribbean, before production halted. The model that was advertised back then as America's most glamorous sports car. Jay Leno has the poster up on the wall of his garage, right above his own Packard Caribbean . That ad was not Packard overpromising and underdelivering.
The most powerful Packard engine The convertible is powered by Packard's largest-ever engine, an overhead-valve V8 with a displacement of 374 cubic inches (6.1 liters). Fitted with dual four-barrel Rochester carburetors, it produced 310 horsepower and 405 pound-feet of torque. In 1956, the Caribbean was the highest output of any American production car.
A Twin-Ultramatic automatic transmission, which featured a futuristic, electronic push-button gear selector pod mounted on the steering column, put the power to the ground through the rear wheels. In fact, pretty much everything was futuristic about the car.
Instead of the traditional steel springs, the Caribbean came with chassis-length torsion bars connecting the front and rear wheels. An electric motor and sensors automatically adjusted shorter leveler bars to keep the car perfectly flat, regardless of passenger weight or luggage, offering a "magic carpet glide.”
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Developed by Dana specifically for Packard Caribbean in 1956, one of the first mass-produced limited-slip differentials were fitted to the car, channeling power away from a slipping wheel to improve handling on slippery roads.
As for the looks, the model came with a striking three-tone paint scheme, separated by thick chrome moldings. It featured dual fiberglass hood scoops, elegant cathedral-style taillights, dual power rear antennas, and a standard Continental tire kit.
The hand-stitched interior featured unique reversible cushions with leather on one side and plush brocade cloth on the other. Unlike competitors where luxury features cost extra, the Caribbean came standard with power steering, power brakes, power windows, dual heaters, a Wonderbar signal-seeking radio, and electronic swiveling power seats. Factory air conditioning was one of the very few options.
Only 539 such units were built before production permanently ended at the factory in Detroit in June 1956, with 276 convertibles and 263 hardtops. So the one in Jay Leno's Garage is one of the 276 that saw the light of day.
Photo: Jay Leno's Garage | YouTube Back then, the Packard Caribbean convertible started at nearly $6,000, the equivalent of roughly $70,000. It was the second most expensive car on the American market, trailing only the ultra-exclusive Continental Mark II.
But that's not what Jay Leno drives on the latest episode. He has driven the Caribbean a gazillion times before. It is the 1902 Model F that he takes out for a spin. The moment he fires up the engine of the 1902 Packard Model F, the car starts vibrating as if an earthquake just started, and the studio fills up with smoke. Once out in the wild of the city, people wave at them, and they wave back.
The vibration is still there, giving them the feeling that it is a wild horse, ready to throw them off. It is actually 12 horses, but all are tamed. Jay Leno feels inspired: " Shift into high and wave bye-bye. " To him, the Packard Model F feels like the perfect car for going out to get ice cream on a Sunday morning
